To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the technique of cascade-cascade reconstruction in the NEVODO Cherenkov water detectors with a spatial lattice has been developed and tested, the energy spectrum of near-horizontal muons with energies from 10 to 1000 GeV has been measured, the energy spectrum and the angular distribution of muons in the energy range of 1–1000 Gev have been obtained.

a technique of cascade-curtain reconstruction in the NEVODO water Cherenkov detector has been developed and used to measure the energy spectrum of near-horizontal muons with energies from 10 to 1000 GeV.

the energy spectrum of cascades in the energy range of 10–1,000 GeV is measured for the first time using a technique based on analysis of Cherenkov light in the NEVODO detector, which is a large water Cherenkov detector with a quasi-spherical geometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for measuring the energy of cascade showers in Cherenkov water detectors.
the development of the NEVOD-DECOR facility for studying extensive air showers.
the development of a technique for measuring the energy spectrum and the energy distribution of cascade showers in the energy range of 10– 1000 GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the results of this study are in agreement with previous studies and the results of the present work are consistent with the results of the previous work.
the energy spectrum of the cascade showers in the range 10–100 GeV is in good agreement with the predictions of the CORSIKA code for a model of hadronic interactions in the atmosphere.

the results obtained are very important for the further development of the NEVOD project and the creation of a large-scale complex of detectors for investigating the extensive air showers of cosmic rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy spectrum of muons is not a good approximation to the data.
we developed a new technique for measuring the energy of cascade showers in the Cherenkov detector.
the cascade shower energy spectrum measured with the NEVOD detector agrees well with the spectrum measured with the L3 experiment at the LEP accelerator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy of a cascade shower is proportional to the number of particles in the cascade shower, which is determined by the number of triggered photomultplier tubes.

the energy spectrum of cascades is described by the power law with the exponent −2.6±0.3, which is in agreement with the results obtained for muon cascades in other experiments and is consistent with the predictions of quantum field theory.
the cascade-shower energy spectrum in water can be reconstructed with a high accuracy.
